# URLCode store

> Operator-installed declarative data store extension for URLCode. Declare
> typed collections in `urlcode.yaml`, mount each with `extension: store`, and
> the extension serves a bounded JSON CRUD API backed by atomically written
> files in an operator-owned directory. No handler code. Delivered as a signed
> executable bundle; not an independent security assessment. Apache-2.0.

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only; never packages, code or credentials)
- `extensions.store: { version: "1", config: { collections: { <name>: { fields, sortable, filterable, readOnly, ... } } } }`
- A mount per collection, e.g. `/api/notes/*: { extension: store, methods: [GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE] }`
- Protect the mount with `policies.extensions.auth` (or another policy) unless the scaffold's
  explicit `--ack store:public-write` was given; an unprotected write mount has no rate
  limiting, abuse protection or multi-tenant isolation of its own.
- The operator wires `storeExtension({directory: '/absolute/operator/path', projectSha256})` in a
  host file loaded with `urlcode serve --host-file /absolute/host.mjs --origin https://...`

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): signed-bundle install, scaffold, the deprecated npm migration path.
- [docs/STORE.md](../../docs/STORE.md): the full HTTP contract, limits and concurrency guarantees.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): trust boundary, locking, `ETag`/`If-Match`, `Idempotency-Key` scoping.

## Do not guess
- No CRUD or persistence code in project `function`/`middleware` routes; declare the
  collection. Those routes run trusted and in-process, but hold no store authority of their own.
- One server process per data directory (an exclusive lock file enforces it); no
  transactions, whole-file atomic writes, last write wins unless a caller sends `If-Match`.
- `sortable`/`filterable` field lists are declared per collection; `?sort=`/`?<field>=` queries
  against an undeclared name are `400`s, not silently ignored.
- The data directory is operator-owned, outside the project, on local disk, not a network
  filesystem; the store creates it `0700` and its files `0600`.
- The `store-schema` signed declarative artifact is a configuration-schema snapshot and
  example only: installing it does not install this executable bundle or grant data access.
